definition: Travel technique for moving across glaciated terrain while managing crevasse and fall hazards.
application: Used on glaciers and snow-covered routes where crevasses or unstable snow may be present.
related_equipment: Crampons; ice axe; rope; harness; crevasse-rescue kit
safety_note: Requires appropriate rope technique, route assessment, and rescue competence.

definition: Connecting members of a climbing party to a rope system so that the team can manage hazards such as crevasses and falls.
application: Common on glaciated terrain and exposed snow or ice routes.
related_equipment: Rope; harness; carabiners; slings
safety_note: Rope spacing and technique must match terrain and hazard conditions.

definition: Rescue techniques for recovering a climber from a glacial crevasse using rope systems, anchors, friction hitches, and hauling equipment.
application: Used after a crevasse fall when a self-rescue or partner rescue is required.
typical_terrain: Glaciers; snow bridges; heavily crevassed terrain
related_equipment: Rope; pulley; prusik cord; ice screws; snow anchors; harness
safety_note: This is a technical rescue skill requiring hands-on training.

definition: Use of an ice axe and body position to arrest or reduce a slide on a snow slope after a slip.
application: Emergency technique on snow slopes where a sliding fall is possible.
related_equipment: Ice axe; crampons
safety_note: Self-arrest is not guaranteed to stop every fall; preventing a fall remains primary.

definition: Climbing steep snow or ice with the front points of crampons engaged in the surface.
application: Used on steep snow, hard ice, and technical alpine terrain.
typical_terrain: Steep snow; hard ice; ice routes
related_equipment: Technical crampons; mountaineering boots; ice axes
safety_note: Requires appropriate crampon-compatible boots and practiced footwork.

definition: Crampon technique in which the crampon points are kept broadly engaged with the surface while moving across less steep snow or ice.
application: Efficient movement on moderate snow and ice where front-pointing is unnecessary.
related_equipment: Crampons; mountaineering boots
safety_note: Technique selection depends on slope angle, surface conditions, and footwear.

definition: Creating or improving footholds in snow or ice to facilitate movement on terrain where existing footholds are inadequate.
application: Used on snow or ice slopes when natural footholds are insufficient.
related_equipment: Ice axe; crampons
safety_note: Energy-intensive and condition-dependent; modern crampon technique often reduces the need for extensive step cutting.

definition: Managing a climbing rope so that a climber can be protected against a fall and controlled during movement.
application: Used on technical rock, snow, ice, and mixed climbing where protection is required.
typical_terrain: Rock; ice; mixed terrain; steep snow
related_equipment: Rope; harness; belay device; carabiners; anchors
safety_note: Belay systems must be matched to the rope, device, anchor, and climbing situation.

definition: Descending a steep section using a rope and a friction or belay device.
application: Used when down-climbing is impractical or when routes require a rope descent.
typical_terrain: Rock; ice; steep snow; technical alpine terrain
related_equipment: Rope; harness; belay/rappel device; locking carabiner
safety_note: Backup systems and anchor quality are critical; this is a technical skill.

definition: Ascending a steep section protected by a fixed rope using a mechanical ascender or friction-based system.
application: Common on steep high-altitude routes where fixed ropes are installed on exposed sections.
typical_terrain: Steep snow; ice; rock; fixed lines
related_equipment: Ascender; harness; carabiner; lanyard
safety_note: Fixed ropes are not automatically safe; inspect the system and use compatible equipment.

definition: Using a friction hitch on a rope as a backup, attachment, or part of a rescue system.
application: Used in rappelling backups, rope rescue, and fixed-rope systems.
related_equipment: Prusik cord; rope; carabiner
safety_note: Friction hitches depend on cord and rope compatibility and correct loading.

definition: Creating a secure point or system to transfer climbing or rescue loads into snow, ice, or rock.
application: Used for belays, rappels, protection, and rescue systems.
related_equipment: Slings; carabiners; ice screws; snow anchors; rope
safety_note: Anchor design must account for direction and magnitude of expected loads.

definition: Using an ice screw as a protection or anchor component in suitable ice.
application: Used to protect or anchor climbing on ice.
related_equipment: Ice screws; rope; carabiners; harness
safety_note: Placement quality depends strongly on ice structure and conditions; requires practical training.

definition: A rope technique in which climbers move at the same time while remaining connected to a protection system.
application: Used on terrain where the party can move together while maintaining protection.
typical_terrain: Easy to moderate rock; snow; alpine ridges
related_equipment: Rope; harness; protection; carabiners
safety_note: Requires experienced judgment because rope management and fall consequences differ from pitched climbing.

definition: A rope-management technique in which the rope between climber and partner is kept relatively short to manage movement on suitable terrain.
application: Used by trained teams on moderate exposed snow or mixed terrain.
related_equipment: Rope; harness; ice axe; crampons
safety_note: Technique is terrain- and skill-dependent and should not be treated as a universal safety method.

definition: Selecting and following an appropriate line through complex mountain terrain using terrain features, maps, weather, and route information.
application: Used throughout an expedition, especially in poor visibility or complex terrain.
related_equipment: Map; compass; GPS; altimeter
safety_note: Route choice must account for objective hazards, weather, and changing conditions.

definition: Recognizing terrain and snow conditions that may indicate hidden or visible glacial crevasses.
application: Used when moving across glaciers and snow bridges.
related_equipment: Rope; probe or pole; map; ice axe
safety_note: Snow can conceal crevasses; visual assessment alone may be insufficient.

definition: Climbing that combines rock and ice or snow in the same technical sequence.
application: Used on alpine routes where rock and ice are interspersed.
related_equipment: Technical crampons; technical ice axes; helmet; rope; protection
safety_note: Mixed terrain creates changing protection and movement demands.

definition: Technical climbing on ice using specialized tools, crampons, and protection.
application: Used on frozen waterfalls, steep alpine ice, and ice-covered faces.
typical_terrain: Steep ice; frozen gullies; alpine ice
related_equipment: Technical ice axes; technical crampons; ice screws; rope
safety_note: Requires specialized training and condition assessment.
source: Petzl ice axes/crampons; BMC winter climbing

definition: Using ice tools and crampons on rock without relying on ice placements.
application: Used on mixed and technical routes where rock sections interrupt ice.
related_equipment: Technical ice axes; crampons; helmet; rope; protection
safety_note: Equipment and movement technique are specialized and route-dependent.
source: Petzl ice axes; Grivel Tech Machine

definition: Managing rope arrangement, spacing, and movement among team members while crossing glaciated terrain.
application: Used to reduce consequences of crevasse falls and manage team movement.
related_equipment: Rope; harness; carabiners; slings
safety_note: Exact rope configuration depends on terrain, team size, and rescue plan.

definition: Using mechanical advantage and rope systems to raise a climber or load from a crevasse.
application: Used during partner or team crevasse rescue.
related_equipment: Pulley; rope; prusik cord; anchors; carabiners
safety_note: Rescue systems require training and must be adapted to the actual situation.

definition: Selecting, placing, and managing protection so that a climbing system can limit fall consequences.
application: Used on rock, ice, snow, and mixed terrain.
related_equipment: Ice screws; slings; carabiners; anchors; rope
safety_note: Protection quality is highly dependent on placement and material conditions.

definition: Planning an ascent by integrating route characteristics, weather, terrain hazards, camps, equipment, timing, and retreat options.
application: Used before and during alpine and high-altitude expeditions.
related_equipment: Map; route information; weather data; navigation tools
safety_note: Plans must remain adaptable because mountain conditions change.

definition: Coordinating movement of a climbing team on exposed terrain while maintaining appropriate protection and communication.
application: Used on exposed ridges, traverses, and steep alpine terrain.
related_equipment: Rope; harness; helmet; protection
safety_note: The appropriate rope method depends on terrain and team competence.
